items.caption:
Why do we dream? What science knows so far.
No settled answer: one review links dreams to mind wandering, threat rehearsal has mixed support, and a back-of-brain hot zone tracks dreaming in REM and non-REM sleep.

items.caption:
An epidemic left people frozen for decades.
Encephalitis lethargica, the "sleeping sickness" of the 1910s and 1920s, left some survivors frozen for decades. In 1969 Oliver Sacks woke some with L-dopa.
Made by Studia with AI tools (text and art); facts checked against the sources on the slides.

items.caption:
Sperm whales may sleep standing up.
Tagged sperm whales spent about 7% of their time drifting vertically near the surface, still and unresponsive. Scientists think these short bouts are sleep.
